scope: All fifty practical engineering manuscripts; full-body editorial review plus targeted verification of claims against primary documentation.
review_type: A second adversarial pass by the writing assistant. This is not an independent human review or proof of human authorship.
verdict: Do not publish this batch yet. Useful topics and mostly sound direction, but many sketches lack the promised runnable scenario or observed result.

ranked_findings.finding: Several examples could mislead a reader copying them: any SQL error counted as permission enforcement, a Drop wrapper had no usable join path, a webhook receipt stored only a hash, and capture tests were credited with policy enforcement.
ranked_findings.action: Corrected the examples and narrowed their claims. Added article-derived CI checks for the permission assertion, task ownership, worker reply, and stored receipt. Live SQL Server permissions, full worker recovery, and gateway policy remain unverified.

ranked_findings.finding: A plan for testing is repeatedly presented where the reader needs a working example, trace, or result.
ranked_findings.action: Complete the specific demonstration recorded for each article before approving it. Passing a small helper test does not establish a whole application or security property.

ranked_findings.finding: The drafts overgeneralized cache misses, left thread-handle drop behaviour ambiguous, or timed an HTTP call without making response-body completion explicit.
ranked_findings.action: Added restore-prefix and immutable-cache nuance; distinguished standard detached thread handles from custom joining destructors; made the timing helper include bounded body consumption.

ranked_findings.finding: The English is readable but sometimes formal, repetitive, or written like instructions to the editor.
ranked_findings.action: Simplified terms and removed internal editorial notes. A later pass should vary the repeated problem/snippet/test-plan/conclusion structure using actual evidence rather than artificial grammar mistakes.

ranked_findings.finding: All fifty remain below the repository 700-word requirement for reviewed clustered articles.
ranked_findings.action: Add useful demonstrations and explanation or make an explicit editorial policy decision later. Do not pad prose or weaken the existing gate during this review. Google does not prescribe a preferred word count.

ranked_findings.finding: Some supporting topics will overlap unless their scenario and outcome are distinct.
ranked_findings.action: Keep each problem narrow and demonstrate its unique contribution. Where no distinct example emerges, update the existing parent or combine the overlapping drafts rather than publish a shorter rewrite.

language.assessment: Mostly clear and accessible to non-native readers, but the repeated instructional cadence can feel machine-produced. This is an editorial judgment, not an authorship determination.

examples_simplified.result cardinality: exactly one result per item key
examples_simplified.positive field selection: allow only intended fields in the log
examples_simplified.operational resolution path: a way for an operator to resolve the outcome

language.next_pass: Start with a real observed failure, keep one worked example, explain its result, and remove repeated generic endings. Preserve necessary technical terms and explain them once. Do not invent personal stories or insert grammar errors to simulate a writer.

length.prose_count_method: Exclude frontmatter, fenced code, inline code, HTML tags, and link targets; count remaining whitespace-separated words.
length.publication_audit_count_method: Match markdownWordCount in scripts/audit-authority-campaign.mjs: exclude frontmatter, fenced code, inline code, and HTML tags; strip Markdown punctuation and retain link-target words.
length.seo_caveat: The 700-word gate is a site policy, not a Google ranking requirement. Original examples and satisfying the reader question matter more than padding.

seo_and_internal_links.strengths: Specific problem-led titles, a defined deeper destination for each article, and related practical subjects.
seo_and_internal_links.remaining: Add original evidence and a distinct answer before indexing. Check existing parent overlap, add reciprocal contextual links only where useful, and review rendered headings and summaries. Fifty new pages alone do not establish SEO strength.

overlap_pairs.distinction: Atomic applied-event claim versus durable acceptance before HTTP acknowledgement.
Caller admission policy versus ownership and release of a retained-byte budget.
Initial read-only rollout versus per-workflow offered and executed capabilities.
Trusted credential selection versus preserving authority across fallback.
Retain the failing input versus ensure a negative test fails for its intended reason.
Concurrency and latency distribution versus control of experimental variables.

verification.new_ci: See the latest Content safety run on https://github.com/mehdiakiki/mehdi-cz/pull/11; this source record does not claim an unobserved result.
verification.existing_coverage: Nine self-contained Rust excerpts plus draft/publication tests, a production build, and private rendering of all fifty. These checks do not validate every sketch.
added_checks: Article 13 task completion, panic, and cancellation request.
Article 18 success, typed job failure, dropped sender, and worker panic.
Article 39 actual PostgreSQL commit, recovered bytes after connection-pool reopen, and duplicate receipt count.
Article 9 compile the exact Tiberius update probe and reject an unrelated transport failure.
limits: No live SQL Server permission or import scenario is claimed.
Reopening a PostgreSQL pool is not a process-crash or power-loss test.
A capture adapter and an offered-tool list do not prove executor authorization or egress policy.
Performance experiments remain unrun unless the article provides its actual evidence.
All builds, tests, and compilation run only through the existing GitHub workflow and its configured runners.

source_checks.supports: Exact and prefix cache restoration, immutable entries, and deliberate new keys.
Borrowing a JoinHandle, detached drop behaviour, abort requests, and observing termination.
Moving fields out of a Drop type is disallowed.
Standard thread handles detach when dropped.
Reading response body data is a separate operation from obtaining the response.
Error 229 denotes object permission denial; column-level denial can differ.
Helpful original evidence and no preferred word count for Google.

articles.title: Database pool full? Check who is holding the connections.
articles.strength_or_correction: Useful first diagnostic question; the pool-acquisition versus query-time distinction is clear.
articles.next_required_edit: Show two concurrent requests against a controlled slow dependency and the actual checkout lifetime before and after the scope change.

articles.title: Keep HTTP calls out of the checkout transaction.
articles.strength_or_correction: Clear checkout scenario and honest limits on cross-system atomicity.
articles.next_required_edit: Show committed stock, pending shipping intent, and recovery at each chosen interruption point. The current sketch does not demonstrate the worker.

articles.title: Don't handle duplicate webhooks with SELECT, then INSERT.
articles.strength_or_correction: The unique claim plus local mutation is a useful narrow application of the parent inbox article.
articles.next_required_edit: Run two deliveries together and show one committed effect. Explain the duplicate outcome with actual stored rows, distinct from article 39 receipt acceptance.

articles.title: Use a separate database account for migrations.
articles.strength_or_correction: The separate migration identity is practical advice, with appropriate effective-permission caveats.
articles.next_required_edit: Add a disposable role setup and observed runtime-role failures for DDL, ownership, and unintended role membership.

articles.title: Make an index earn its place in a write-heavy table.
articles.strength_or_correction: The write cost and HOT-update qualification are directionally sound.
articles.next_required_edit: Provide the actual schema, query plans, update workload, index sizes, and measured comparison; do not ask readers to accept an unrun performance conclusion.

articles.title: Put two tenants in your authorization tests.
articles.strength_or_correction: Two tenants make a better failure case than an isolated happy path.
articles.next_required_edit: Include the complete authenticated request fixture and read/update/list checks, so the test proves the application boundary rather than just a SQL predicate.

articles.title: Don't return success before the commit finishes.
articles.strength_or_correction: Commit acknowledgement and an uncertain commit outcome are kept separate.
articles.next_required_edit: Make a commit fail after the mutation and show both the HTTP result and final stored state. Retain the uncertain-outcome recovery explanation.

articles.title: A background SQLite import should leave room for normal saves.
articles.strength_or_correction: The advice respects SQLite single-writer behaviour without promising that WAL removes contention.
articles.next_required_edit: Demonstrate bounded batches with a second connection making normal saves, including busy outcomes and an explicit import recovery point.

articles.title: Run reports with a database account that cannot write.
articles.strength_or_correction: Fixed the negative test so a connection error cannot pass as a permission denial.
articles.next_required_edit: Compile the exact Tiberius probe and reject an unrelated transport failure in CI. A real SQL Server run must still show allowed reads, error 229 for the configured table-level denial, and unchanged fixture state.

articles.title: A rejected import row needs somewhere to go.
articles.strength_or_correction: A rejected-row ledger is a concrete operational problem; removed internal editorial instructions from the prose.
articles.next_required_edit: Implement the reject record and corrected-row replay against the intended engine, including duplicate retry and credential handling.

articles.title: Release the mutex before calling a remote API.
articles.strength_or_correction: The lock-scope example gives a clear action; replaced abstract resource-contract wording.
articles.next_required_edit: Add a controlled remote wait and a second task to prove the mutex is released while the first operation waits.

articles.title: Decide what happens when the queue is full.
articles.strength_or_correction: Queue-full behaviour is a useful policy choice; simplified the admission-contract heading.
articles.next_required_edit: Exercise the selected reject/wait/durable-accept policy and show the caller-visible result. Keep byte ownership in article 19.

articles.title: Don't detach a task just to hide a slow request.
articles.strength_or_correction: Fixed the Drop wrapper so its JoinHandle can be awaited by borrowing it; clarified that abort is a cancellation request.
articles.next_required_edit: Run the article-derived completion, panic, and cancellation cases. A cleanup or external side-effect claim needs a separate controlled fixture.

articles.title: Set a byte limit before collecting a response body.
articles.strength_or_correction: One of the strongest small examples: limit enforcement and overflow have direct boundary checks.
articles.next_required_edit: Add the reader-visible check output and an async HTTP adaptation with decompression and timeout limits if the article promises an HTTP recipe.

articles.title: One request should not start a thousand tasks at once.
articles.strength_or_correction: Acquiring a permit before spawn addresses a real source of retained work.
articles.next_required_edit: Demonstrate the maximum number of started tasks and retained inputs under load, including cancellation and a downstream limit.

articles.title: An Arc clone can keep old data alive longer than you expect.
articles.strength_or_correction: The Arc example is small enough to inspect and has a direct executable check.
articles.next_required_edit: Show the observed strong counts and explain the corresponding service ownership path. Avoid turning counts into an unmeasured memory diagnosis.

articles.title: Don't use a metrics counter to decide who can book the last place.
articles.strength_or_correction: The atomic reservation example is a useful contrast with a metrics-only counter.
articles.next_required_edit: Include the concurrent test result and clearly delimit process-local reservations, release ownership, and the multi-replica case.

articles.title: Send worker failures back to the caller.
articles.strength_or_correction: Typed job errors and a closed reply are clearly separated in the exact snippet.
articles.next_required_edit: Run success, business error, dropped sender, and panic cases. Still add a receiver-disconnect example for work that can commit a write.

articles.title: A queue of 100 messages can still use too much memory.
articles.strength_or_correction: The retained-byte problem is distinct from the number of queued messages.
articles.next_required_edit: Replace the arithmetic-only demonstration with an owned byte reservation released on receive, cancellation, failure, and drop. A passing fits_budget test does not establish a queue memory bound.

articles.title: Check whether Drop is making your Rust request slow.
articles.strength_or_correction: Corrected the thread-handle wording: standard JoinHandle drop detaches; a custom wrapper may block in Drop.
articles.next_required_edit: Show a measured or instrumented destructor on a request path and the resulting task delay, with the cleanup moved to an explicit owner.

articles.title: Keep the broken input before you fix the bug.
articles.strength_or_correction: The saved failing input is a clear practical improvement over a one-off fix.
articles.next_required_edit: Include one concrete original input, the intended requirement, and the regression assertion. Redact or synthesize private input rather than inventing a personal incident.

articles.title: A test should fail for the reason you meant.
articles.strength_or_correction: A strong teaching point: an error result alone does not prove the intended protection.
articles.next_required_edit: Turn one of the negative examples into a complete test with an allowed-path control and a deliberate unrelated failure. Cross-link the corrected article 9 example.

articles.title: Don't fix a flaky test with a longer sleep.
articles.strength_or_correction: Signals are more useful than longer sleeps, but the test currently depends on helpers the reader cannot run.
articles.next_required_edit: Provide the worker and synchronization setup, an outer timeout for a missing signal, and a deterministic assertion about state rather than elapsed sleep.

articles.title: Don't put a timestamp in the dependency cache key.
articles.strength_or_correction: Qualified the blanket cache-key claim: compatible restore prefixes can restore an older cache, and immutable entries sometimes justify a new suffix.
articles.next_required_edit: Show the actual workflow and cache-hit/restore output for the dependency use case. Distinguish correctness boundaries from cache refresh policy.

articles.title: Check the lockfile change before blaming the new Rust compiler.
articles.strength_or_correction: Strongest real incident in the batch: linked CI evidence records lockfile drift from crypto-bigint 0.7.8 to 0.7.9.
articles.next_required_edit: Add a compact before/after log excerpt and explain why the committed lockfile plus --locked resolves this observed case without claiming all Rust upgrades are dependency drift.

articles.title: Test generated code from an empty output directory.
articles.strength_or_correction: An empty generated-output directory is a useful way to reveal hidden build inputs.
articles.next_required_edit: Provide a complete CI job or script and demonstrate the expected failure after removing one required generator input.

articles.title: Keep the debug symbols for the binary you actually shipped.
articles.strength_or_correction: Keeping symbols matched to the shipped binary is useful, but the draft stops before a reproducible investigation.
articles.next_required_edit: Add exact profile and symbol-retention commands, build identity, artifact storage, and a sample symbolized trace from the matching artifact.

articles.title: Measure tail latency before raising request concurrency.
articles.strength_or_correction: Fixed the timing sketch so completion includes a bounded response body, not only response headers.
articles.next_required_edit: Run a controlled workload and publish throughput, queue time, tail latency, failures, and cancellations for each concurrency setting. Do not label a proposed experiment a result.

articles.title: Change one performance variable at a time.
articles.strength_or_correction: The controlled comparison is understandable after replacing factorial jargon and internal editorial notes.
articles.next_required_edit: Publish the four configurations, raw observations, run order, and limits. Without measurements the article remains a method, not a demonstrated optimization.

articles.title: Should generated API clients live in their own Rust crate?
articles.strength_or_correction: The generated-client crate split has a plausible benefit, with useful maintenance caveats.
articles.next_required_edit: Measure the same representative edits before and after the split and show dependency boundaries. Explain when another crate adds cost instead.

articles.title: Keep provider status strings out of UI components.
articles.strength_or_correction: The provider-status mapping is a concrete boundary with an executable unknown-state case.
articles.next_required_edit: Show how the application presents and recovers Unknown, plus one compatibility test for a newly introduced provider value.

articles.title: Don't turn every provider 429 into a customer 500.
articles.strength_or_correction: It correctly distinguishes provider/account rate limits from a blanket customer error.
articles.next_required_edit: Add sanitized provider response fixtures and the resulting retry/user outcomes, including missing or unusable retry guidance.

articles.title: Choose one layer to own retries.
articles.strength_or_correction: The attempt-budget helper has direct boundary checks; simplified the concluding rule.
articles.next_required_edit: Demonstrate actual attempt counts across application and SDK layers, including a deadline, jitter policy, and a non-idempotent write.

articles.title: After a timeout, check the outcome before repeating the write.
articles.strength_or_correction: The uncertain-write scenario is useful; simplified the operational-recovery wording.
articles.next_required_edit: Show the provider lookup or idempotency mechanism returning the stored outcome after a timeout. A local timeout cannot establish remote rollback.

articles.title: Don't repair an entire integration inside a GET request.
articles.strength_or_correction: The small GET path versus recoverable repair work is a useful design decision.
articles.next_required_edit: Add the response contract, durable repair job, deduplication, and failure/retry fixture. Distinguish ordinary safe reads from hidden repair writes.

articles.title: Make API cursors opaque and bind them to the query.
articles.strength_or_correction: Query-bound cursors are a concrete correctness issue; simplified the encoding explanation.
articles.next_required_edit: Provide encoding, integrity verification, expiry, and query comparison, then reject a cursor reused with another tenant/filter/order.

articles.title: Put the tenant in the cache key, not just the record ID.
articles.strength_or_correction: A strong small reproduction: identical external IDs remain separate across tenant keys.
articles.next_required_edit: Show caller-supplied tenant validation and cache invalidation through the service path. The key test alone does not prove authorization.

articles.title: A bulk response must say which items succeeded.
articles.strength_or_correction: Per-item outcomes are practical advice; replaced result-cardinality jargon with exactly one result per item key.
articles.next_required_edit: Add a mixed response fixture with out-of-order results, duplicate or missing keys, and a retry of only unresolved items.

articles.title: A webhook response should follow durable acceptance.
articles.strength_or_correction: Fixed the receipt to store recoverable payload bytes alongside pending state; a hash alone cannot reconstruct the work.
articles.next_required_edit: Run commit/reconnect and duplicate receipt checks. Still demonstrate real worker recovery, conflicting-payload rejection, and chosen interruption points; reconnecting a pool is not a process-crash test.

articles.title: Give repair scripts a preview before they write.
articles.strength_or_correction: Preview-before-write is useful when the preview is bound to the eventual write conditions.
articles.next_required_edit: Provide the complete preview/apply command, stale-preview refusal, authorization, and partial-failure record with synthetic data.

articles.title: Start an internal AI tool with read-only access.
articles.strength_or_correction: Read-only rollout is a useful first capability boundary and acknowledges data exposure.
articles.next_required_edit: Demonstrate the actual available tool set, executor denial of guessed writes, and tenant-scoped reads. A rollout plan is not a sandbox guarantee.

articles.title: The model should not choose whose credentials it uses.
articles.strength_or_correction: Credential choice belongs in trusted code; the draft only models this choice so far.
articles.next_required_edit: Implement the trusted user/account lookup and reject model-supplied credentials or another tenant account. The type definitions alone do not enforce this.

articles.title: Log the tool decision without copying the customer's document.
articles.strength_or_correction: The logging advice is sensible; simplified positive-field-selection wording.
articles.next_required_edit: Show the logger adapter, bounded fields, and captured output with injected secrets, newline content, oversized values, and error paths.

articles.title: Only offer tools that belong to the current workflow.
articles.strength_or_correction: The offered-tools example is executable, but it only checks the offered list.
articles.next_required_edit: Invoke a hidden write directly against the executor and prove it is denied. Keep workflow scoping separate from article 41 initial rollout.

articles.title: A denied tool call must leave no side effect.
articles.strength_or_correction: The side-effect assertion is the right target; simplified the permission-change wording.
articles.next_required_edit: Supply the real gateway and effect spy behind the current test sketch, and exercise denial through authorization, approval, fallback, and retry paths.

articles.title: A fallback model must not get wider permissions.
articles.strength_or_correction: Preserving authority through fallback is a useful distinct problem; removed formulaic invariant wording.
articles.next_required_edit: Run primary failure followed by fallback through the same trusted context and executor, then assert a prohibited effect did not occur.

articles.title: Your agent test should not be able to send a real email.
articles.strength_or_correction: Corrected the overclaim: a capture adapter stores an intended message; it does not establish authorization or approval enforcement.
articles.next_required_edit: Show test startup wiring, absence of production credentials, gateway policy cases, and egress enforcement. The small capture test proves message retention only.

articles.title: Even a trusted tool needs an output limit.
articles.strength_or_correction: A trusted producer can still return too much data; the distinction is useful.
articles.next_required_edit: Implement the stream reader, decompression and byte/token handling, truncation signal, and early stop. A limit configuration type does not prove enforcement.

articles.title: Don't delete the eval case that made the release look bad.
articles.strength_or_correction: A useful companion to ordinary regression testing, with concrete evaluator fields.
articles.next_required_edit: Supply the regression case, evaluator, expected decision/effect, and a known bad variant that fails. Separate deterministic checks from stochastic model runs.

articles.title: An overall eval score can hide the workflow you broke.
articles.strength_or_correction: The synthetic table is clearly labelled and its totals and slice regression are checked in CI.
articles.next_required_edit: Show one actual release gate using per-workflow failures, sample counts, and explicit high-risk criteria. Do not imply the small synthetic slice estimates production risk.
